question.problem:
Suppose ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{9}$ is an I.I.D random sample where ${X}_{i}∼\text{Bernoulli}(\theta )$ with unknown probability of success $\theta .$ For a particular sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{9},$ you're given that there are $4$ successes. Find the log-likelihood function of the sample.

*Hint: The probability mass function for a Bernoulli random variable is given by* 

$$
f(x)={\theta }^{x}(1-\theta )^{1-x},\,x=0,1.
$$

current_example.problem: Suppose $X_1,X_2,\ldots,X_{10}$ is an I.I.D random sample where $X_i\sim \text{Bernoulli}(\theta)$ with unknown probability of success $\theta.$ For a particular sample $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_{10},$ you're given that there are $7$ successes. Find the log-likelihood function of the sample.
current_example.worked_solution:
Recall that if $X_1, X_2, \ldots, X_{n}$ are independent and identically distributed discrete random variables with probability mass function $f(x; \theta),$ where $\theta$ is an unknown parameter, then the log-likelihood function of a random sample $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡L(\theta ) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({\prod }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i};\theta )) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡(f({x}_{i};\theta )).\end{aligned}
$$

We are given a sample of $n=10$ independent Bernoulli random variables with unknown parameter $\theta.$ Therefore, the probability mass function is

$$
f(x;\theta) = \theta^x(1-\theta)^{1-x}, \qquad x=0, 1.
$$

We can calculate the log-likelihood function as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡({\theta }^{{x}_{i}}(1-\theta )^{1-{x}_{i}}) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡({\theta }^{{x}_{i}})+\operatorname{ln}⁡((1-\theta )^{1-{x}_{i}}) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +(1-{x}_{i})\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta ) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta {\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}+\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta ){\sum }_{i=1}^{n}(1-{x}_{i}) \\  & =S\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +(n-S)\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta )\end{aligned}
$$

where $\displaystyle S = \sum_ {i=1}^n x_i$ is the number of successes in the sample.

Finally, since there are $7$ successes in the sample, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & =7\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +(10-7)\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta ) \\  & =7\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +3\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$
